newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends weaker as DOEs fail to stem losses.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends weaker as DOEs fail to stem losses.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended weaker on Wednesday after the approval of a new U.N. oil-for-food deal with Iraq, and despite fresh U.S. inventory data which was less bearish than expected, traders said.
July Brent ended the day 19 cents a barrel lower at $18.71, after June gas oil's close earlier at $168.75, a fall of $1.25 a tonne on the day.
"The market still looks bad, I'm afraid," one IPE broker said. "It is a continuation of weakness from U.S. data we had earlier."

Dealers said the approval of the U.N. oil-for-food deal with Iraq, which allows the country to sell another $2 billion of oil over 180 days, had been widely anticipated and was already factored into the price.
Latest data from the U.S. Department of Energy (DoE)showed a weekly build in crude oil stocks of 4.2 million barrels and a gain in gasoline inventories of 900,000 barrels.

But these builds were smaller than those reported late on Tuesday by the American Petroleum Institute (API,) which showed an 8.4 million barrel build in crude stocks and a 2.9 million barrel rise in gasoline stocks.
"There was a small recovery on the back of the DoEs in the afternoon but there was not enough in it to negate the overall negative picture," one IPE dealer said.

He said that chartists were looking closely at the key support level of $20.00 a tonne on July NYMEX crude oil. The market touched this level earlier in the day and then rebounded and stood 10 cents above that level at 2025 GMT.
But he added that Brent would also now be encountering support at current levels. "From about $18.75 we are entering layers of support which go all the way down to $18.00."
